title: BABOL: A Software-Defined NAND Flash Controller
problem: NAND Flash controllers require custom hardware designs to support package-specific optimizations, making them error-prone, non-portable, and difficult to update. Rigid hardware controllers cannot readily adapt to new Flash generations and optimization techniques emerging in research.
motivation: Accelerates SSD development and prototyping by decoupling Flash-specific optimizations from fixed hardware, enabling faster exploitation of advancing Flash technologies.
method: BABOL provides generic hardware building blocks that can be flexibly composed via software to express package-optimized Flash operations. Two FPGA implementations were created and validated with commercial Flash packages to demonstrate the architecture's effectiveness.
key_novelty: Software-defined Flash controller that enables programmable composition of generic hardware primitives for different packages and optimizations, eliminating the need for rigid custom controller designs.
contributions: Software-defined Flash controller architecture with generic hardware building blocks
Two FPGA implementations demonstrating the design's feasibility
Open-source controller implementation and novel software programming environment
Validation with multiple commercial Flash packages showing flexibility outweighs marginal performance and area costs
limitations: Not discussed in abstract; comparison against specific prior controller designs not provided.
